bib.title: Mixture-of-Transformers: A Sparse and Scalable Architecture for Multi-Modal Foundation Models

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed; plot axis text in figure bodies (Figures 6, 9, 12, 15-19, 24-26) is fragmentary and not used except the step-matching ratios; figure images not viewed.

question: Can giving each modality its own non-embedding transformer parameters, with global self-attention over the whole interleaved sequence, cut the pretraining compute of multi-modal (text, image, speech) generative models at equal FLOPs?
hypothesis: Modalities occupy distinct regions of feature space and conflict in a dense model, so rule-based modality-specific parameters (no learned router) should train faster than a dense model and than learned-routing MoE.
contributions: MoT: a sparse multi-modal transformer that unties FFN, attention projections (Q, K, V, O) and LayerNorm per modality while keeping global self-attention, with the same FLOPs as the dense counterpart

Pretraining from scratch of thirteen instances (three at 7B) in Chameleon (text+image autoregressive), Chameleon+Speech and Transfusion (text autoregressive, image diffusion) settings, against dense and MoE-4x baselines
Ablation of which components to untie, and a leave-one-modality-out analysis of modality sharing
Preliminary hybrid of MoT with MoE-4x in the text tower
System profiling of throughput, GPU scaling and wall-clock time on AWS A100s

method.summary: Each transformer layer routes tokens by their known modality to separate Q/K/V/O projections, FFN and LayerNorm weights, then runs one global self-attention over the full sequence. Dense, MoT and MoE-4x (Expert Choice routing) models are pretrained from scratch with matched FLOPs at several scales in three settings, and compared by training loss, step matching, validation loss and generation metrics.
method.task: multi-modal pretraining (text, image, speech) with autoregressive and diffusion objectives

datasets.name: Chameleon mixed-modal training data
datasets.size: roughly equal amount of text and image tokens; 0.168 to 0.377T tokens seen per run (Table 1)
datasets.source: same data and tokenizers as Chameleon Team (2024); images tokenised into 1,024 discrete tokens with a pre-trained VQ tokenizer (Gafni et al., 2022)

datasets.name: Obelisc, MS-COCO (Karpathy test), Flickr30k (Karpathy test), Shutterstock held-out sets
datasets.split: held-out validation; COCO and Flickr30k used for text-to-image and image-to-text conditional perplexity
datasets.source: Laurencon et al. 2023; Lin et al. 2014; Plummer et al. 2015; Shutterstock

datasets.name: SpiRit-LM speech data (People's Speech, Voxpopuli English, LibriLight, Multilingual LibriSpeech English, Spotify)
datasets.size: 16,404 + 23,166 + 55,308 + 44,585 + 57,290 hours; 1.2B + 1.6B + 4B + 3.2B + 4.2B speech tokens after dedup, plus 0.5B and 0.7B text tokens in the two speech+text sets
datasets.source: Nguyen et al. 2024 (Table 2); speech tokens from an in-house DinoSR variant, vocabulary 500, 40ms per token (25Hz)
datasets.preprocessing: speech-only plus interleaved speech/text in SpiRit-LM format; speech set combined with Chameleon text-image set at sampling ratio 1:6

datasets.name: LibriLight (LL60K) and People's Speech (PPL30K) held-out sets
Transfusion text corpus
datasets.size: 2T-token Llama 2 corpus (sampled); 0.5T tokens/patches sampled in total at 1:1 text:image

datasets.name: Shutterstock licensed images and captions
datasets.preprocessing: centre-crop and resize to 256x256; VAE with 8x8 spatial downsampling; BOI/EOI tokens around image sequence; caption first 80% of the time

datasets.name: Wikipedia, C4 held-out; CC12M; MS-COCO
datasets.size: 20 million held-out text tokens (Wikipedia/C4); 30,000 randomly selected COCO validation prompts for FID/CLIP
datasets.split: CC12M held-out for diffusion validation loss; COCO Karpathy test for CIDEr

models.name: Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT)
models.params: 37M, 94M, 443M, 880M, 1.5B, 7B (Chameleon/Speech); 163M, 760M, 1.4B, 7B (Transfusion); sized to match the dense FLOPs, sizes quoted are activated parameters
models.architecture: decoder-only transformer with per-modality Q,K,V,O, FFN and LayerNorm weights and global self-attention
models.tokenizer: Chameleon text and image tokenizers; Llama 2 tokenizer in Transfusion

other.Transfusion extra: U-Net patch encoder/decoder adds a fixed 0.27B parameters at every size; image = 256 continuous tokens; lambda = 5
other.FFN: analysis assumes SwiGLU FFN with 3D^2 parameters and 4D^2 attention parameters

models.name: MoE-4x (also MoE-2x, MoE-3x at small scales)
models.params: same activated parameters as dense; more total parameters
models.architecture: dense model with 4 experts per MLP and Expert Choice routing (Zhou et al. 2022)

other.eval: evaluated with the same EC routing as training (not causal), which may leak future tokens; caption metrics excluded for this reason

models.name: MoT + Text MoE-4x
models.architecture: MoT whose text FFN is replaced by a 4-expert MoE layer

training.objective: Chameleon: autoregressive next-token loss on text and image tokens (and speech tokens); Transfusion: L_LM + lambda * L_DDPM with lambda = 5, cosine noise schedule
training.optimizer: Transfusion: AdamW (beta1=0.9, beta2=0.95, eps=1e-8); Chameleon and Speech settings: null
training.lr_schedule: Transfusion: cosine decay to 1.5e-5; Chameleon settings: null
training.batch_size: Tokens/batch 1.05M to 3.15M in Chameleon runs (Tables 1, 3); 2.10M in Transfusion; per-GPU batch 12 down to 2 sequences
training.tokens: Chameleon 0.168T to 0.377T (most 0.252T; 7B 0.377T); Transfusion 0.524T in Table 4, 0.5T in text
training.hardware: AWS p4de.24xlarge instances (NVIDIA A100); Chameleon 32 to 384 GPUs, Transfusion 128 to 256 GPUs (Tables 1, 4); FSDP full shard, PyTorch 2 compiler
training.compute: FLOPs matched to the dense baseline in every comparison; no GPU-hours stated
training.wall_clock: relative only (MoT reaches dense image loss in 47.2% of GPU time, 256 GPUs, 443M Chameleon)

other.fine_tuning: 7B MoT and dense fine-tuned on an internal visually appealing dataset (details not given) and 7B MoT on 8k image-editing examples; fine-tune hyperparameters not stated
other.table_note: Table 4 prints 7B Tokens/Batch as '2.10N' (typo for 2.10M); Transfusion section text says 'five different sizes' but lists four

inference.decoding: Transfusion: 250 diffusion steps; no classifier-free guidance unless noted; CFG 5 for 7B example images, CFG 1.6 for the 7B COCO-30k FID of 8.14
inference.samples: COCO-30k: 30,000 prompts for FID and CLIP score; seeds not stated

metrics.name: Training / validation loss and step matching s
metrics.definition: fraction of the dense model's training steps (or FLOPs, or GPU time) a model needs to reach the dense model's loss; validation loss on held-out Obelisc, COCO, Flickr30k, Shutterstock, LL60K, PPL30K
metrics.unit: fraction of dense steps / loss in nats

metrics.name: Diffusion validation loss
metrics.definition: diffusion loss on held-out CC12M, following SD 3

metrics.name: FID
metrics.definition: zero-shot Frechet Inception Distance on 30,000 COCO validation prompts

metrics.name: CLIP score
metrics.definition: alignment of generated COCO images with prompts

metrics.name: CIDEr
metrics.definition: caption quality on the Karpathy test split of MS-COCO
metrics.unit: score (printed as 0.320 in figures, 40.6 in text for 7B)

baselines: MoE-4x (Expert Choice), plus MoE-2x and MoE-3x at small scales
partial untying variants (FFN only; FFN + QKV)
1T-token dense model with richer data (FID 9.22 at guidance 1.6)
eval.protocol: single runs per configuration as far as the text shows; no seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests stated. Sparse model sizes are activated parameters. All runs FLOPs-controlled and pretrained from scratch.

availability.data: Chameleon, Transfusion and SpiRit-LM data are Meta-internal or cited, not released here; Shutterstock is licensed; the internal fine-tuning set is not described

evidence.quote: optimize them using AdamW (β1 =0.9, β2 =0.95, ϵ =1e-8) with a learning rate of 3e-4, warmed up for 4000 steps and decaying to 1.5e-5 using a cosine scheduler
Training steps were set at 160,000 for smaller models (37M to 443M) and 120,000 for larger models (880M to 7B).

results.claim: In the Chameleon 7B setting MoT matches the dense model's validation losses with 55.8% of the training FLOPs.
results.setup: Chameleon 7B, text and image autoregressive, 120k steps dense, Obelisc/COCO/Flickr/SSTK validation losses, FLOPs controlled, one run
results.quote: This indicates that MoT requires only 55.8% of the training FLOPs to match the dense model’s validation metrics, offering substantial computational savings.
results.note: The abstract and Figure 5 also say 44.2% reduction in FLOPs; 45.5% of steps for global training loss

results.claim: At 7B in Chameleon, MoT needs only 34.8% of the dense model's steps to match image training loss.
results.metric: steps to match dense image loss
results.quote: requiring only 34.8% of the dense model’s training steps to match final loss
results.note: Fig 6 plot label shows s = 0.348 for MoT image at 7B

results.claim: Adding speech, MoT reaches the dense model's speech performance with 37.2% of the FLOPs at 7B.
results.metric: FLOPs fraction to match dense speech loss
results.setup: Chameleon+Speech 7B, speech validation loss on LL60K and PPL30K
results.quote: MoT reaches baseline speech performance in 37.2% of the FLOPs (f).
results.note: Speech training loss matched in 22.9% of steps; across 443M to 1.5B, 15.1% to 33.6% of steps

results.claim: In Transfusion, a 760M MoT using half the FLOPs of a 1.4B dense baseline beats it on CLIP (0.214 vs 0.206).
results.setup: Transfusion, 760M MoT vs 1.4B dense, COCO 30k prompts, no classifier-free guidance, 250k steps
results.quote: Image quality improved, as evidenced by CLIP (0.214 vs 0.206) and FID (21.145 vs 24.688) scores (Figure 11c,d).

results.claim: Same comparison: FID 21.145 for the 760M MoT against 24.688 for the 1.4B dense model.
results.setup: Transfusion, 760M MoT vs 1.4B dense, COCO-30k, no CFG
results.note: Sec 3.4.3 prints different 760M numbers from Fig 12: FID 15.75 vs 25.58 (MoT vs dense at 760M) and CLIP 0.214 vs 0.202; this paper does not explain the 760M dense baseline discrepancy (1.4B dense 0.206 / 24.688 in Fig 11 vs 760M dense 0.202 / 25.58)

results.claim: A 7B MoT matches the dense image diffusion loss in about 30% of the steps in Transfusion.
results.metric: steps to match dense image loss
results.quote: MoT achieves equivalent image pre-training loss to the dense model in only 30% of the training steps.
results.note: Abstract says one third of the FLOPs; Fig 10e plot label s = 0.374

results.claim: 7B MoT improves COCO-30k FID to 8.14 at guidance 1.6, against 9.22 for a dense model trained on 1T tokens of richer data.
results.setup: Transfusion 7B MoT, 0.5T tokens; baseline trained on 1T tokens with richer data (a different model, not controlled)
results.quote: we compute the COCO-30k FID at a guidance level of 1.6 and obtain a score of 8.14
results.note: The baseline is a different training set and token budget

results.claim: 7B MoT more than triples caption learning speed, ending at CIDEr 40.6 vs 31.5 for dense.
results.quote: achieving a final score of 40.6 versus 31.5
results.note: Fig 10h prints 0.406 vs 0.315 (same numbers on a 0-1 scale)

results.claim: MoT reaches the dense model's image training loss in 47.2% of GPU time and text loss in 75.6%, while MoE-4x is 1.7x slower on image.
results.setup: Chameleon, 443M, 256 A100 GPUs on AWS p4de.24xlarge, FSDP, PyTorch 2 compile; authors expect results to vary by cluster
results.quote: MoT matches the dense model’s image training loss in 47.2% of the total GPU training time and continues to improve thereafter (Figure 19b).
results.note: Abstract attributes the same numbers to the '7B' model in the introduction; Sec 6.2.2 says 256 GPUs and the horizontal-scaling study uses 443M, so the model size for Fig 19 is not stated clearly

results.claim: MoT's relative benefit grows with GPU count: steps to match dense image validation loss fall from 42.1% (16 GPUs) to 21.6% (256 GPUs).
results.metric: steps to match dense (image val loss)
results.setup: Chameleon 443M, Obelisc, global batch and tokens scaled with GPU count at constant step count
results.quote: the percentage of training steps required for MoT to match the dense model decreases from 42.1% (16 GPUs) to 21.6% (256 GPUs).

results.claim: Untying attention Q,K,V on top of FFN untying saves about 33.3% of FLOPs for image and 10% for text on held-out Obelisc.
results.setup: Chameleon 880M ablation (Table 5), 120k steps; LayerNorm untying then adds negligible gain
results.quote: this leads to approximately 33.3% FLOPs saving for the image modailty and 10% FLOPs saving for the text modality compared to only performing untying in the feedforward module.

results.claim: MoE-4x loses its image-modality advantage as scale grows and is unstable on speech validation, where MoT is consistently better.
results.setup: Chameleon and Chameleon+Speech, 37M to 7B; the MoE-4x baseline uses Expert Choice routing evaluated non-causally
results.quote: where it underperforms the dense baseline in speech validation loss, despite outperforming it in speech pre-training loss.
results.note: Authors offer routing imbalance and overfitting as unverified explanations

results.claim: Added parameters per layer: MoE adds more than 3(E-1)D^2, MoT adds 7(K-1)D^2, so MoT has a lower parameter-to-FLOPs ratio when K is small.
results.setup: SwiGLU FFN with 3D^2 and attention with 4D^2 parameters, hidden = embedding = D
results.quote: In contrast, MoT incurs an added parameter count of (K−1)×(|ATTN|+|FFN|) = 7(K−1)D2.

results.claim: In the Transfusion setting, text gains from MoT are marginal to none, unlike Chameleon where MoT matched dense text loss in 54.6% to 66.2% of steps.
results.setup: Chameleon 37M to 7B text training loss versus Transfusion 163M to 7B
results.quote: In Chameleon, MoT required only 54.6% to 66.2% of training steps to match the dense model’s text modality training loss.

limits: FLOPs-matched comparisons in pretraining loss only; no downstream benchmark accuracy or human evaluation of generations, and Transfusion text results show little gain.
Single run per configuration; no seeds, variance or significance tests reported.
Chameleon and Speech optimizer, learning rate, schedule, warmup and precision are not stated; Chameleon data are Meta-internal, so exact reruns are not possible.

MoE-4x baseline uses Expert Choice routing evaluated non-causally, which can leak future tokens or mis-balance experts, so the MoE comparison is confounded (authors say so); caption metrics for MoE excluded.
Wall-clock and GPU-scaling results come from one AWS A100 setup; authors expect relative speeds to vary by cluster.
Models of at most 7B trained on 0.5T tokens (Transfusion), well below state-of-the-art image generators; scaling beyond this is future work.
Hybrid MoT + MoE-4x results are preliminary; MoE-4x training-loss gains did not carry to validation in Transfusion.
LayerNorm untying was tested only on top of FFN and attention untying.

Inference deployment (mixed-modality batching, padding) is discussed but not measured; routing overheads (CPU-GPU sync, sequential modality processing) are noted but not on the critical path in their setup.
Fine-tuning data (internal) and recipe are undescribed; qualitative image comparisons only.

terms.definition: a sparse multi-modal transformer that introduces modality-aware sparsity for all non-embedding transformer parameters (FFN, attention projections, LayerNorm) while keeping global self-attention
plot of the training steps a sparse model needs to reach the dense model's loss at each dense step
text and images (and speech) as discrete tokens, all trained with autoregressive objectives
text trained autoregressively and images as continuous patches trained with a diffusion objective in one transformer
parameters per FLOP, which governs training throughput through communication overhead

lineage.note: Chameleon setting and data; MoT is a drop-in replacement for its dense transformer

lineage.work: Transfusion: Predict the next token and diffuse images with one multi-modal model
lineage.note: Transfusion setting, data and dense baseline

lineage.work: MoMa: Efficient early-fusion pre-training with mixture of modality-aware experts
lineage.note: FFN-only modality untying, reproduced as an ablation arm

lineage.work: CogVLM: Visual expert for pretrained language models
lineage.note: modality-specific attention on top of a pretrained LLM, text output only
concurrent, frozen text LLM plus trainable image transformer with global attention

lineage.work: SpiRit-LM: Interleaved spoken and written language model

lineage.note: variant used as in-house speech tokenizer
diffusion validation loss as a predictor of quality

figures.caption: Mixture-of-Transformers architecture for multi-modal generative AI.
figures.why: Shows per-modality QKV, FFN and LayerNorm with one shared attention across Chameleon and Transfusion inputs.

figures.caption: Pre-training acceleration of MoT for 7B Chameleon multi-modal model.
figures.why: Step-matching curves and the 55.8% FLOPs checkpoint comparison.

figures.caption: In the Transfusion setting, a 760M MoT model outperforms a 1.4B dense baseline across key image generation metrics, while using only half the FLOPs.
Ablation results of modality untying in different transformer components in the Chameleon setting.
figures.why: Shows which components matter (FFN, then attention, LayerNorm negligible).

figures.caption: Speed advantage of MoT in wall-clock time (Chameleon Setting).
figures.why: Translates FLOPs savings into GPU time and shows MoE-4x slowdown.

code.snippet: a = GlobalAttn(x, {θ^m_attn}); h_i = x_i + LayerNorm^{m_i}_attn(a_i); output_i = h_i + LayerNorm^{m_i}_ffn(FFN(h_i, θ^{m_i}_ffn))

problems: Plot axis labels in the extracted text are fragmentary, so figure-only values were not used beyond printed captions and legends.

Inconsistent numbers: Sec 3.4.3 gives 760M FID 15.75 vs 25.58 and CLIP 0.214 vs 0.202, while Sec 3.4.2 and Fig 11 give 760M MoT FID 21.145 vs 24.688 (1.4B dense) and CLIP 0.214 vs 0.206. Fig 10g shows 7B FID values 18.862 and 19.502 for MoT vs dense.
Sec 3.4.1 says 'five different sizes' but lists four; Table 4 prints '2.10N' for 7B tokens/batch.

Abstract and introduction place the 47.2%/75.6% wall-clock result with the 7B model while Sec 6.2.2 describes 256 GPUs and the horizontal-scaling study uses 443M; the model size for Fig 19 is not stated clearly.
